claims.text: TaNbHfZrTi is an example of a Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy.
The initial solid alloy has the potential to undergo a liquid-phase transition.
A perturbation scheme using a liquid-trained moment tensor potential can replace full thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method applies in a high-temperature, near-melting multicomponent liquid regime.
An MTP training set can capture chemical short-range order.
An MTP training set containing liquid configurations can capture the relevant multicomponent liquid structure.
MTP captures complex liquid structure more accurately than EAM in Ta-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
MTP captures the relevant multi-body interactions in a chemically disordered liquid.
MTP represents these interactions more efficiently than EAM.
The MTP enables perturbation-based free-energy estimation without integrating over the full phase space.
The perturbation scheme will provide a 10-100 times computational speedup relative to thermodynamic integration.
The perturbation scheme will resolve free-energy differences with less than 5% error.
Standard ab initio thermodynamic integration is computationally expensive for this application.
Empirical EAM potentials fail to capture the relevant multicomponent liquid structure.
The method is valid only for Ta-based refractory high-entropy alloys whose training data cover the liquid phase and chemical short-range order.
The method fails when liquid configurations are absent from the training set.
Underrepresentation of liquid configurations can cause potential extrapolation errors.
Accuracy depends on the MTP's ability to represent multi-body interactions in the disordered liquid.
Deviation from thermodynamic-integration free energies by more than 5%, or failure to reproduce liquid radial-distribution features, would falsify the hypothesis.
Testing a composition outside the training set can assess extrapolation robustness.
